item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J00575","case1_error":"Assumes an unsupported zero starting inventory and reports cookie balances inconsistent with removals and returns.","case2_error":"Allocates half the sugar to the cake, although two cake layers require twice the sugar of the cupcake batch.","reason":"The first invents an initial inventory and inconsistent balances; the second incorrectly partitions a total among unequal shares.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00576","case1_error":"Assumes an unsupported zero starting inventory and reports cookie balances inconsistent with removals and returns.","case2_error":"Treats the $2 price for five cans as the price per can.","reason":"Invalid inventory initialization and tracking differ from confusing a bundle price with a unit price.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00577","case1_error":"Evaluates the correctly written subtraction 80 − 16 as 40 instead of 64.","case2_error":"Omits the factor of 250 papers delivered daily, calculating recycling revenue for one paper per day.","reason":"The first is a numerical evaluation error; the second omits a required multiplicity from the weight calculation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00578","case1_error":"Uses the 12-apple excess as the green count, omitting the red-count baseline when forming the total.","case2_error":"Sets the combined pink-and-orange count equal to 3x, omitting the orange baseline x.","reason":"Both form a combined total while omitting one baseline contribution required by the stated comparison.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J00579","case1_error":"Introduces $3,000 in taxes without calculation or support from the stated 20% profit tax.","case2_error":"Adds the five lost points instead of subtracting them, inflating Jimmy’s remaining points.","reason":"An unsupported tax amount differs from an explicitly incorrect relation that treats a loss as a gain.","judgment":"different"}]}
